bottom_line: With the CLARITY Act stalled in the Senate, U.S. regulators (CFTC, SEC, OCC) are advancing crypto market-structure and capital-markets access piecemeal via existing authority, expanding derivatives products and stablecoin bank charters rather than waiting for comprehensive legislation.

updates.headline: CFTC broadens no-action relief for crypto wallet software
updates.what_happened: The CFTC's Market Participants Division issued Staff Letter 26-25, expanding a no-action position previously limited to Phantom Technologies to cover any qualifying 'passive software' provider (wallets, DeFi front ends, apps) that routes users to CFTC-registered derivatives venues without requiring introducing-broker registration. The relief lasts until the Commission finalizes formal rulemaking and does not shield providers from other laws such as money-transmission or DOJ criminal statutes.

updates.headline: Coinbase, Kalshi, Bitnomial file for single-stock perpetual futures
updates.what_happened: Coinbase Derivatives, Kalshi, and Kraken-linked Bitnomial each filed proposed rule changes with the SEC/CFTC on September 18 to list cash-settled, no-expiry perpetual futures on individual U.S. stocks and ETFs (Apple, Tesla, Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, SPY, QQQ among proposed underliers). CFTC approval remains pending for all three filings, and the products would give price exposure only, without ownership, dividend, or voting rights.

updates.headline: Bastion wins conditional OCC national trust bank charter
updates.what_happened: Stablecoin infrastructure provider Bastion received preliminary conditional OCC approval to convert its New York trust charter into a national trust bank charter (Bastion Platforms National Trust Company), covering GENIUS Act-compliant stablecoin custody, wallets, payment infrastructure, and white-label issuance. The charter bars deposit-taking and lending and is not FDIC-insured, joining Ripple, Circle, and BitGo among firms securing similar federal stablecoin charters.
